details: Nature walks provide direct experiential learning of local flora and fauna.
Community elders possess immense traditional wisdom regarding bird calls and plant identification.
experiments_or_examples: Guided nature walks with experts like Dr. Raghu and Maniram Chacha

details: Herbs: Small plants with soft, green, non-woody stems (e.g., wheat, mustard, mint).
Shrubs: Medium-sized plants with hard woody stems branching near the base (e.g., rose, lemon, hibiscus).
Trees: Tall plants with thick, hard main woody trunks (bole) branching high above ground (e.g., mango, neem, banyan).
experiments_or_examples: Classifying garden plants by stem hardness and branching height

details: Climbers: Plants with weak stems that use tendrils or external structures to climb upright (e.g., pea, money plant).
Creepers: Plants with weak stems that spread horizontally along the ground (e.g., pumpkin, watermelon).
experiments_or_examples: Observing tendrils wrapping around wooden stakes

details: Animals possess specialized body organs adapted to walk, fly, swim, or crawl.
Birds use legs for land movement and modified forelimbs (wings) for flight.
Fish swim using streamlined bodies and fins.
Ducks paddle in water using webbed feet with skin connecting toes.
experiments_or_examples: Observing locomotion of ants, goats, pigeons, ducks, and fish

details: Adaptation is the presence of specific physical features or habits enabling survival in a specific habitat.
Mountain trees (Deodar) have conical shapes and needle-like leaves to shed snow easily.
Desert plants (Cacti) have fleshy stems for water storage and spines (modified leaves) to reduce transpiration.
experiments_or_examples: Comparing mountain pines with desert cacti and lotus in ponds
